info.title: Kolibri
info.description:
Generated by `scripts/openapi.mjs` from the entity registry and the route files. Do not edit by hand —
`npm run openapi` rewrites it, and `npm run check:openapi` fails if it has drifted from the tree.

Every entity in the registry has the same five routes and a real schema below. The hand-written routes
are listed with their method and parameters only: their bodies live in the handlers, and a guess would be
a claim nothing checks.

token.description: An API token from **Settings → API & MCP**, or `POST /api/tokens`. A `read` token is refused on every write.

session.name: kolibri_session
session.description: What the web app uses, from `POST /api/auth/login`.

action_kind.description: What it does when it fires.

action_patch.description: For `set_fields`: the patch to apply to the task that triggered it.

apply_to_generated.description: Whether the rule also applies to tasks an automation created. Off by default.

exclude_actor.description: Leave out whoever caused the trigger — you rarely review your own work.

link_kind.description: How the new task is linked back to the one that triggered it; '' for none.

once.description: Fire at most once per task, rather than on every entry.

project_id.description: Null means every project in the workspace.

ref.description: User id for `user`, team id for `team`, role name for `role`.

trigger_days.description: For `due_in`: how many days before the due date.

entries.description: `taskId → [start, due]`, with `null` for a date the task did not have.

approved.description: What was signed off, if anything. `0` means nobody has approved a number and the plan is the only figure there is — which is honest, and different from an approved budget of nothing.

currency.description: ISO 4217, upper case. One currency per budget and no conversion anywhere: a rate is a fact about a day, and a report that silently picks today's to add up last year's is worse than one that declines to add them at all. Two currencies in a portfolio are shown as two totals.

project_id.description: The project that owns it, or null when it is shared. See `coversProject`.

projects.description: The projects it covers. Empty means *every* project, not none.

share.description: Basis points of the cost. The list sums to 10000.

allocations.description: Empty inherits the line's split; see `allocationsFor` in `budget.ts`.

line_id.description: The plan line this pays for, or null when nothing planned it.

reference.description: Invoice or purchase-order number — what an auditor asks for.

spent_on.description: The day the money moved, which is not the day somebody typed it in.

share.description: Basis points of the cost. The list sums to 10000.

allocations.description: Whose figures this lands in. Empty is unallocated — see `Allocation`.

amount.description: Per occurrence, not for the whole window. See `recurrence`.

starts_on.description: The line's own window. Null falls back to the budget's period.

line_id.description: One line, or empty for every line matching `category` / `kind`.

factor.description: Basis points of the original amount. 12000 is "20% more".

delta.description: Added after the factor, in minor units. Negative takes money out.

shift_months.description: Move the line's window by whole months. Negative pulls it earlier.

drop.description: Take the line out of this scenario entirely.

note.description: Why. Shown beside the number, because a number alone is not an argument.

adjustments.description: What to do differently. Applied in order; a line named twice takes both. See `applyScenario` in `budget.ts`.

weights.description: How much of an unsigned cost this scenario carries, in basis points, per confidence level. Absent means "all of it" — the plan as written.

invite_policy.description: Who may change that list: anybody in it, or only its creator and workspace admins.

members.description: Who can see it. Empty means the workspace, not nobody.

name.description: Lowercase and dash-joined. Empty for a direct conversation, which has no name of its own.

project_id.description: Set to tie the channel to a project; it then follows that project's visibility.

prefix.description: The text immediately before and after it, for disambiguation.

anchor.description: The passage this comment is about, for a comment made on a selection. A quote with its surroundings rather than an offset, because an offset is wrong the moment somebody types a word above it. See `anchor.ts`.

guest_name.description: Who said it, when nobody here said it. Set only on a comment left through a public share link, where there is no account behind it. Never verified, and shown as unverified everywhere: a name in a box is a name in a box.

amount.description: Per occurrence, like a budget line's. `0` means nobody has priced it.

line_id.description: The plan line this is charged to, so the two can be reconciled.

live_from.description: When it joined the estate and when it leaves. These, not `status`, are what decide whether it is in the landscape on a given day — see `livenessOn`.

location.description: Where it physically is: a region, a data centre, a rack.

parent_id.description: The server this runs on, or the account this seat belongs to.

projects.description: Projects that depend on this. A dependency, not a cost split — the split lives on the budget line, and this answers "who breaks if it goes".

reference.description: What it is called where it lives — a hostname, an account, an ARN.

project_id.description: The project that owns it, or null when several run it. See `coversProject`.

projects.description: The projects that run it. Empty means *every* project, not none.

Error.description: Every failure answers in this shape, with a matching HTTP status.

message.description: A sentence for a person, which may name the thing that was wrong.

options.description: Choices, for the two select kinds. Ignored by every other kind.

required.description: A prompt, not a gate. Nothing refuses to save a task without it: a task created offline, by a rule or over the API would otherwise be impossible to write, and a required field that only sometimes applies teaches people to type a full stop into it.

show_in_table.description: Offer it as a column in the table view.

value.description: Always text on the wire; `readFieldValue` turns it back into its kind.

reporter.description: What the reporter typed about themselves. Neither is verified.

task_id.description: The task it became, once somebody accepted it.

baseline.description: Where it stood before anybody started, if that is known. Null is honest and common — most KPIs are defined halfway through. Progress then runs from the first reading instead, and the screens say which.

decimals.description: Where the decimal point goes, for every value on this KPI and its targets. Values are integers scaled by `10 ** decimals`, for the reason money is: 99.95 stored as a float and summed twice is not 99.95, and these figures get averaged and compared against a target. `parseMeasure` and `formatMeasure` are the only two places a decimal point exists.

project_id.description: The project that owns it, or null when it is shared. See `coversProject`.

projects.description: The projects it covers. Empty means *every* project, not none.

unit_label.description: The word after the figure when `unit` is `number`. "Tickets", "customers".

module_id.description: The milestone this is due by. When set, its date wins over `due_on`.

address.description: The address itself, folded to lower case. `support@calendoora.de`.

folders.description: Which folders to read. Empty means INBOX alone.

members.description: Who may read it, when `access` is `members`. Empty means nobody.

name.description: What to call it on screen. Empty means show the address.

sync_days.description: How far back to fetch on the first pass. 0 means everything.

username.description: Usually the address, sometimes not — Microsoft and a few hosts differ.

edited_at.description: Stamped by the server when the body changes, never taken from a client.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers, for a short thread inside the stream.

project_id.description: The project that owns it, or null when several share it. See `coversProject`.

projects.description: The projects it covers. Empty means *every* project, not none.

project_id.description: The project doing the work, when somebody has made one.

channel_id.description: The conversation, when it is about something somebody said in one.

project_id.description: Where to go when it is about neither one task nor one page.

v.description: Format marker, so a later shape can be told from this one.

a.description: Agent ids, interned — they repeat on every run otherwise.

body.description: The same text as a CRDT, which is what makes two people typing at once a merge rather than a race. Merged rather than replaced on write; see `text-crdt.ts`. Null on a page nobody has edited since this existed.

content.description: What the page says. Derived from `body` whenever there is one, so that everything reading a page — search, export, the share document, the renderer, the API — carries on reading plain text.

is_template.description: A page kept as a starting point rather than as content.

watchers.description: Who asked to hear about changes — a page has no assignees to fall back on.

default_view_id.description: The saved view this project opens on. On the project rather than a flag on the view, so that two people pinning two different views merge into one answer instead of two rows both claiming to be the default.

is_container.description: A project that only holds other projects. A flag rather than a separate "folder" entity, because a folder would need its own sync, permissions, trash, REST and MCP surface — and would make every tree in the app ask whether a parent is a folder or a project. A container is an ordinary project that has said it has no work of its own, so it keeps all of that for free and can be turned back at any time.

parent_id.description: The project this one sits under. Nesting is for reading, not for access.

working_days.description: Which weekdays this project works on, as `Date.getUTCDay()` numbers. On the project rather than the workspace because a support rota and an office team can genuinely disagree inside one company. Empty means every day counts.

reason.description: `manual` if somebody pressed the button, `retention` if the clock did.

amount.description: Per hour, in minor units. See `Minor`.

currency.description: ISO 4217. A workspace mixing two is shown two totals, never a sum.

starts_on.description: Valid from this day. There is no end: the next row's start is the end.

user_id.description: Whose hour. Null is anybody's — the workspace's own default.

lag.description: Working days of breathing room, on a `blocks` link. Never negative — see `schedule.ts`. Ignored on the other kinds, which say nothing about time.

allow_comments.description: Whether strangers may leave a note on a shared page. Off by default: an unauthenticated write is a thing somebody opts into, not a default.

expires_at.description: Epoch millis, or null for a link that does not expire on its own.

token.description: Server-side only: the secret in the URL.

allowed_roles.description: Who may move a task *into* this column. Empty means anybody who can write. Workspace roles, so "only a lead signs work off" is one entry.

wip_limit.description: How many tasks may sit here at once. 0 means no limit.

recurred_from.description: The task this one was created from, when it is a repeat.

recurrence.description: How this repeats, if it does: `daily`, `weekly:2`, `monthly`. The next one is created when this one is finished, not on a calendar. A weekly task nobody did four times is one task that is late, not four.

assignees.description: Always assigned on top of whatever an automation resolves.

due_in_days.description: Days from creation; null leaves the due date empty.

project_id.description: Null means the whole workspace can use it.

subtasks.description: One sub-task per line, created with the task.

target_project_id.description: Null means "the project the source task is in".

minutes.description: Whole minutes. Nobody logs seconds and everybody argues about decimals.

spent_on.description: The day the work happened, which is not always the day it was entered.

started_at.description: Epoch millis while a timer is running, null otherwise.

contract_start.description: When the contract runs to. The date a renewal is a surprise without.

notice_days.description: How many days before `contract_end` you have to give notice. Its own field rather than a line in the note, because it is the one thing about a contract that has a *deadline* attached: the day you stop being able to leave is `contract_end` minus this, and nothing can compute that from prose.

field.description: Custom field answers: the field's id, then the answers that pass. Two reserved tokens let a filter ask about a field with no list of options — `''` is "nothing here" and `'*'` is "something here". See `fields.ts`.

not.description: The same questions, asked the other way round. `Filters` is otherwise a conjunction of "is one of", which cannot say *not* — and "everything except the done column" is the second thing anybody wants from a filter. A field named here excludes rather than includes; for a field that holds a list (assignees, labels) a task is excluded when **any** of its values is named.

shared.description: 0 keeps it to its owner; 1 offers it to everyone who can see the project.

show_done.description: Whether completed and cancelled tasks are part of the view.
